Discovers live zero-cost tool-capable models by intersecting OpenCode Zen and models.dev over HTTPS, persists only the last successful intersection for restart fallback, and bidirectionally translates compatible OpenCode and Hermes tool schemas, calls, choices, and replayed history while Hermes executes tools locally. No OpenCode CLI, Node.js, npm, or npx dependency. Disclosure — prompts, tool schemas, tool results, and other conversation content leave the machine for OpenCode and the selected model provider; model availability, retention, data use, and permission are governed by their current terms.

name: omnivoice
description: OmniVoice TTS provider for Hermes Agent

name: opaque-composer
description: Keep the desktop composer solid while scrolling so conversation text stays readable.

name: openai-compatible
description: GPT Image through CLIProxyAPI, New API, or any OpenAI Images-compatible gateway, with gateway-aware errors and requested-vs-returned size reporting. Disclosure — sends image prompts and any source images (local files, data URLs or public HTTPS URLs) to the OpenAI-compatible gateway base_url you configure, authenticated with OPENAI_COMPAT_IMAGE_API_KEY.

name: openalex
description: Scholarly search, citation traversal, grouped counts, and fulltext access through OpenAlex with session spending limits.

name: openltm
description: Long-term memory for Hermes agents, stored in a local SQLite database. FTS5 full-text search with optional vector (sqlite-vec) recall, importance-weighted decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture: a declarative rule engine classifies corrections, constraints, preferences, decisions, and agent-discovered facts from a conversation and stores each one as a distilled, self-contained fact. Runtime notifications and read-only OpenLTM tool requests are excluded by named guards so ops noise never becomes memory. No cloud, no telemetry, no API keys required; optional Gemini/OpenAI/Ollama providers for embeddings. MIT licensed.

name: openmail
description: Gives a Hermes agent its own email address. Inbound mail wakes the agent over a websocket, replies go out in-thread, plus tools for sending, reading and provisioning inboxes.

name: openrouter-picker
description: One install: the Desktop model picker and the OR Picker composer provider. Checking a model here is what the composer lists. Disclosure — the optional OpenRouter management key is stored in plaintext in Desktop localStorage; the plugin reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY from your environment, Hermes secret store or HERMES_HOME/.env and sends it only to openrouter.ai (credits, usage, and the Test-model button, which spends credits).

name: openrouter-voice
description: OpenRouter speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers for Hermes Agent (stt.provider / tts.provider = openrouter).

name: openspec
description: OpenSpec CLI tools for spec-driven development workflows

name: optmem-hermes
description: Independent Hermes integration of Victor Taelin's OptMem design: local, append-only memory with regex/BM25 recall and a bounded wake digest. Hybrid and guarded OptMem-only modes; verified migration and rollback. Local by default. Compaction is manual unless auto_nap is enabled. Optional LLM summaries run only when both auto_nap and llm_summary are on; they send memory blocks to the configured provider via host-owned authentication and may incur token costs. Summaries are lossy, raw records remain recoverable, and conflicts are not resolved automatically. Wake consumes model context. See README for upstream attribution. Disclosure — memory is stored locally under HERMES_HOME; optional auto_nap+llm_summary sends stored memory lines to the user's configured model provider; the optmem-only mode (explicit CLI with --yes) disables Hermes' built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md injection after a verified backup.

name: orbit-desktop
description: Your workspace, shaped by your agent: a bundled browser desktop powered by Hermes. Describe the workflow you need; the agent can rearrange windows and panes, customize appearance, build versioned sandboxed web apps, and refine your workspace with scoped control, previews and checkpoints. Illustrated examples show a project-specific COCS 3D asset viewer and OmniVoice experiment bench; these example apps and their backends are not bundled. Includes permission-controlled desktop agent-reply notifications (generic alerts while Orbit remains open; browser/OS restrictions apply) and 100,000-character chat messages, guidance and drafts. Includes Devplan Studio for guided interviews, specifications, phased devplans and circular-development handoff exports. Optional conversational interviews require explicit service setup and a working Hermes provider login, and send project context to that provider. Includes 14 distinctive interface presets including Nous Atelier, with local wallpapers, themed icons and taskbar treatments. Agent chats include inline expandable tool activity, running/completed/failed summaries, an activity strip, a workspace agent overview and responsive toolbar controls. Missing tool-call IDs are explicitly uncorrelated. Embedded apps retain their own styling. Includes a reviewed GitHub app catalog with immutable source pins and a portable Live Telemetry package. Catalog sync (operator-run scripts/orbit_catalog.py, never triggered by the Hermes tool or at register) reads the entry list from the upstream repo's main branch at sync time and downloads third-party static app bundles at their per-entry commit pins; installed UI runs in a sandboxed iframe and never executes backend code. Optional telemetry backend staging downloads pinned Python; execution requires explicit host-code trust and separate private authenticated HTTPS setup. Backend code runs with owner privileges, not a sandbox. Disclosure — adapter talks only to the configured local Orbit server (loopback, Bearer capability from runtime_dir); mutations off by default. Optional orbit.py setup runs npm ci / node. Bundled VNC/Xpra launchers use the Orbit page's hostname and scheme; optional Linux apps require separate provisioning. Optional api.typesafe.ai requests require explicit consent and a user-supplied key. The 0.2.7 web app's opt-in Show tools panel displays tool call arguments and results for the current Hermes conversation, fetched from the local Orbit server and local Hermes session API and kept in the browser only. The Nous Atelier theme contains Nous Research logo artwork and is unofficial; Orbit is not affiliated with Nous Research.

name: orcaslicer
description: Prepare, slice, preflight and export 3D prints with stock OrcaSlicer profiles. Includes explicit printer upload/control, camera snapshots and monitoring through supported protocols. Protocol and hardware limits are documented. Independent of OrcaSlicer and Nous Research. Disclosure — executes the installed local slicer and exposes printer upload, start, pause, resume and cancel; agent-supplied confirmation is not independent human authentication. Printer/camera credentials are read from ORCA_*/HERMES_ORCA_* environment variables named in tool arguments (HTTPS required unless allow_plaintext_credentials is set); plugin state lives in ~/.hermes-orca (HERMES_ORCA_HOME), outside HERMES_HOME.
title: OrcaSlicer for Hermes

name: osv-ref
description: @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: context references: attach a vulnerability record from OSV.dev to a message (summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details, references), with package data merged from up to four alias records. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id> only (the referenced id and up to four of its alias ids leave the machine); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @cve:, @ghsa: and @osv: reference providers.

name: parallel-search
description: Free web search and page fetching through Parallel's hosted MCP, with a setup skill bundled. No account or API key required. Queries and requested URLs are sent to Parallel. Adds direct MCP tools alongside Hermes's native web providers.

name: parcel-deliveries
description: Track package deliveries with the Parcel app (parcelapp.net). List what's on the way, add tracking numbers and look up carrier codes, with a built-in guard for Parcel's strict rate limits. Disclosure — sends tracking numbers, descriptions and optional postcode/order email to api.parcel.app (Parcel Premium API key); the model can add deliveries to the user's Parcel account (add-only, capped at 20/day); caches delivery lists in plugin-data.

name: parlor
description: Rooms where AI agents of any vendor talk to each other. A room is a URL; agents join, read and post over plain HTTP, with no accounts and no sign-in. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package: the parlor skill plus the hosted parlor MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no authentication, 8 tools). Disclosure — hosted unauthenticated MCP connector at parlor.sh/mcp (tool set is server-controlled, not pinned) plus a curl fallback; messages the agent writes go to parlor.sh or the server in a given room URL and rooms are public to anyone with the link; room tokens are stored under ~/.local/state/parlor; the skill may keep background wait loops running.
title: Parlor.sh

name: parrotnotes
description: Find, search, summarize and save insights for your ParrotNotes in-person meeting notes through the hosted ParrotNotes MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 + DCR), with the parrotnotes workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/). Disclosure — hosted-only connector with no local code: every tool call goes to the vendor's remote MCP server at mcp.parrotnotes.app (OAuth via a Supabase auth backend); note titles, transcripts and insights from the user's ParrotNotes account are pulled into the session context, and text the model passes to save_note_insight is written to that account. OAuth must be enabled with `hermes mcp add parrotnotes --url https://mcp.parrotnotes.app/mcp --auth oauth`; the bundled mcp.json alone yields 401.

name: pcs-security-tls-posture
description: Read-only audit of local TLS posture — certificate validity, key strength, deprecated protocols, weak cipher suites, and the certificate each server's configuration points at. Disclosure — reads a fixed list of system certificate and nginx/Apache config paths under / (or a caller-supplied prefix); makes no network connections and runs no subprocesses. If the sibling plugin pcs-security-core is installed, its copy of the shared contract is loaded in preference to the bundled one.

name: pep-ref
description: @pep:<number> context references: attach a Python Enhancement Proposal to a message (status, type, authors, Python version and its first section, usually the Abstract), or one section with @pep:<number>#<section>, with PEP number and title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to peps.python.org only (the PEP index and the referenced PEP's page; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally); keeps the index in memory for an hour; no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @pep: reference provider.

name: pinned-folders
description: A Pinned tab in the Desktop sidebar that files your pinned chats into nested folders: drag to order and nest, folder colors, right-click menus (including Unpin), unread/working badges on collapsed folders, a filter box, open-folder-as-tabs, and layout export/import via the clipboard. Layout stays local to the app; pins belong to the backend. SDK-only build (desktop/plugin.js); no network.

name: pixel-worlds
description: Watch your agents inhabit pixel-art realms in Hermes Desktop, with imported scenes and a minimal PW Agents display.

name: plan-mode
description: Enforced per-session plan mode: /planmode on blocks mutating Hermes tools dispatched through pre_tool_call (writes outside .hermes/plans, terminal, code execution, delegation, MCP) until you /planmode approve the plan. Fails closed. Enforced in the classic CLI on every supported Hermes; gateway, TUI and Desktop are enforced from Hermes v2026.9.24 (0.21.5, which carries hermes-agent commits 5943347a2a and 35fdb4608a) and refuse /planmode on on older builds. The plan_mode tool lets the agent enter plan mode itself (on/status/off; approval stays /planmode approve); behind Tool Search the model finds it via tool_search. Disclosure: Codex app-server native exec and TUI side agents bypass pre_tool_call and are not enforced. Disclosure — reads two private Hermes internals without modifying them (gateway.run._gateway_runner_ref via sys.modules to detect a gateway process, and PluginContext._manager.home_path to learn its profile), both guarded with fallbacks; creates .hermes/plans/ under the session working directory; the plan_mode tool's off action ends only a plan mode the agent entered itself. No network access, no shell, no self-update.
title: Plan mode

name: pocket-watch
description: Dashboard-only cron companion: a Pocket Watch pane showing cron jobs by schedule (daily/weekly/monthly), a health view of run outcomes and consecutive failures, a timeline, and maintenance actions — a read-oriented window onto the scheduler rather than another agent-facing toolset. Disclosure — the pane's API reads the cron jobs file under HERMES_HOME to render schedules and run history; it registers no tools, hooks or middleware, performs no network I/O and holds no credentials.

name: pricewin
description: Live hotel and flight prices from Booking.com, Agoda, Trip.com and Traveloka through the PriceWin MCP server (Streamable HTTP at mcp.price.win, no account or key), with the pricewin-travel-search skill and inline hotel/flight cards for the Desktop transcript bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/ + desktop/). Booking is a request the hotel confirms; nothing is ever charged. Disclosure — connects to the hosted PriceWin MCP server at mcp.price.win (no key); search arguments including a verbatim excerpt of the user's request go to it, and four of its twelve tools act on bookings (request_booking sends guest details to the hotel, cancellation needs a token emailed to the guest); nothing is charged.

name: prism
description: Prism OpenAI-compatible inference with long-context DeepSeek models.

name: privacy-gateway
description: Local Presidio-based PII pseudonymization for Hermes model requests and tool results with an encrypted profile-scoped alias vault. Disclosure — PII detection runs locally with Presidio and the spaCy en_core_web_lg model, which you install manually; alias mappings are stored encrypted in the Hermes plugin DB under HERMES_PRIVACY_GATEWAY_KEY; requests are blocked when the engine cannot load; tools outside rehydrate_tool_allowlist receive alias tokens, not plaintext.

name: profile-pane
description: Disclosure — copies .env key values (and opt-in auth.json backups) between profiles; rewrites other profiles' SOUL, memory and config.yaml. Cross-profile config pane with copy+manifest reconcile and per-group scope.

name: prompt-enhance
description: Rewrite a composer draft outside the chat and put the finished prompt back in the field. A prompt library keeps saved prompts, and a one-call model pick does not change the session.

name: prompt-enhancer
description: A composer button for Hermes Desktop that rewrites a rough draft into a structured prompt (task / scope / constraints / output shape) and restores the original on a second click. One stateless gateway call, preserves @file and /command chips, per-session state. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體.

name: prompt-optimizer
description: Model-aware prompt rewriting with quality scoring, analytics, and coaching. Disclosure — the default auto mode rewrites every user message of 5+ words through your configured model (one extra LLM call per turn) before the agent sees it.

name: prompt-pocket
description: Local prompt library for Hermes Desktop. Save, edit, search, and copy named prompts for manual use, with validated JSON import/export and IndexedDB storage. Does not read or modify composer drafts, send messages, or make network requests.

name: prompt-snippets
description: Prompt snippet library for the Hermes Desktop composer: a quick-pick overlay styled after the app's own slash menu (own shortcut), plus a management view with drag reordering, group tags and import/export. Inserts into the focused session, not the active one. UI in EN / 简中 / 繁體. v1.8.0 is fully SDK-only: the quick-pick overlay renders as an official Popover anchored to the plugin's own contributed node and all draft writes go through the host composer draft API. No local network; v1.6.0+ adds local JSON import/export via the system clipboard.

name: prompt-studio
description: Step-by-step prompt builder for Hermes Desktop (F4): option cards per step with AI suggestions, then an AI-written final prompt sent to or placed in the composer through host.composer (Hermes Desktop 0.21.5+). Tuned for Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. AI calls go through its own auxiliary task (auxiliary.prompt_studio) via the dashboard plugin API; sends no temperature. No external network beyond the configured provider; preferences in ctx.storage. Disclosure — on opening in an existing chat (default on, toggle in Studio Settings) it reads the last 8 user/assistant turns (plus any compaction summary) of that session from state.db, redacts secrets and sends up to 8k chars to the configured auxiliary model for a short summary used in step suggestions; draft and form answers go to the same auxiliary model; no other network.

name: prompt-tray
description: Saved chat prompts — click a tray item to insert it into the Hermes composer. Review / Plan / Explain defaults, then your own. No API keys. Disclosure — inserts prompts through Hermes Desktop's internal hermes:composer-insert event (not a public SDK API); stores prompts in $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/prompt-tray/prompts.json; no network.

name: protean-model-sync
description: Fleet-wide provider and model presets with CLI and Hermes Desktop support. Disclosure — writes model/provider keys into the config.yaml of the profiles you select (backup taken first).

name: protean-ordaprompt
description: Jev-style comparative classifier for OrdaPilot. It compares all topic labels and session choices in one batch, including new-topic, ambiguous, and new-session options. It uses calibrated score and margin gates, weighs continuity against context cost and contamination, and abstains when uncertain. OpenRouter is optional for provisional new-label proposals and disabled by default.

name: protean-subagent-viewer
description: Read-only Hermes Desktop pane for live and past delegated subagent workers.

name: provider-copy
description: Copy provider API keys (and provider base-URL overrides) from one profile onto other profiles — a one-time, explicit copy from a desktop page. Per-profile missing/present badges, fill-missing by default with an explicit overwrite opt-in. OAuth sign-ins and messaging bot tokens never travel; values never cross back in responses.

name: provider-status
description: Status-bar quota tracking for 17 providers: Tavily, OpenCode Go, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), OpenRouter, Grok (xAI), Codex (OpenAI), OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Cerebras, Moonshot Kimi, MiniMax, Google Gemini, Hugging Face, Mistral, and Qwen. DeepSeek and GLM show peak/off-peak gauges and countdowns. Includes OAuth and multi-key pools. This edition does not rotate Hermes environment keys on exhaust. Codex and Grok checks use their CLI client identity and user-agent.

name: provider-usage
description: Per-provider quota and balance readout in the Hermes desktop status bar. Per-provider chips with eye toggles, a popover with every quota window, reset times, balance and key-cap amounts, near-limit amber tint, a desktop notification per threshold crossing, and burn-rate projections (ETA to reset or depletion). Providers: OpenCode, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, plus Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Nous, Z.AI, Kimi, MiniMax and DeepSeek when configured. Disclosure: credentials are resolved read-only (Hermes account-usage helpers for Codex/Claude/Copilot/Nous, else the provider env key or its CLI auth file) and never serialized; only the provider endpoints listed in the README are called; the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity. No subprocesses, no telemetry, no self-updater. Disclosure — resolves provider credentials read-only (Hermes account-usage helpers, provider env keys, else the vendor CLI login files ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json) and sends each only to that provider's usage endpoint; the GitHub Copilot check presents the VS Code / Copilot client identity.

name: pstack
description: Engineering rigor stack: poteto-mode orchestrator with 7 playbooks (new-feature, bugfix, refactor, testing, one-shot, migrate, explore), plus how, architect, interrogate, swarm, and unslop skills.

name: pushary
description: Phone notifications, questions and approvals through Pushary's native Hermes approval transport, with optional per-tool gates. Disclosure — approval transport and per-tool gates hand dangerous-command approvals to whoever holds the devices or Slack channel paired to your Pushary account (fails closed); messages queued in the Pushary app or Mac notch are injected into the next turn as operator instructions; sends session events with a hashed hostname on every turn, redacted tool-error text (max 3 per session) and redacted gated-tool arguments to pushary.com.

name: pushover-hermes-plugin
description: Pushover as an outbound-only gateway platform, plus opt-in agent lifecycle notifications (finished, questions, errors, approvals, kanban blockers) via Pushover and/or native notify-send, managed with /notifications. Disclosure — sends HTTPS requests to api.pushover.net only, carrying your Pushover app token, user key and notification text (when lifecycle notifications are enabled, excerpts of agent replies, clarify questions, approval commands and kanban block reasons; PUSHOVER_NOTIFY_QUESTION=minimal suppresses all but kanban reasons); send_message can address any Pushover user or group key; runs notify-send (argv, no shell) when native notifications are enabled; writes an unrotated log under $HERMES_HOME/logs and settings.json under $HERMES_HOME/plugin-data, and $HERMES_HOME/.env only from the interactive setup wizard. Outbound-only, no inbound or approval path, no telemetry, no background processes.

name: qdrant
description: Dense semantic memory for Hermes, stored in a Qdrant collection you host. Each turn becomes one point — user and assistant text verbatim, no LLM summarization step — embedded on-device at 384 dimensions with fastembed (ONNX; the default install is 206 MB of runtime dependencies with no torch, versus ~1.2 GB when sentence-transformers was a hard dependency) and recalled by cosine search with an optional session_id payload filter, so a result quotes what was actually said. Registers 7 tools: qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert, qdrant_recall, qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_forget (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all), and md_search (local markdown knowledge index). An optional progress display (off/minimal/verbose) reports stored and recalled counts in the CLI. sentence-transformers is selectable on GPU hosts; both backends produce identical vectors for all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so switching backends needs no re-embedding. A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to no new memories instead of crashing, and is_available()/check_backend()/unavailable_reason() distinguish a misconfiguration from a dead server. Hybrid dense+sparse RRF search and INT8 quantization exist in _backend.py but are not on the live path. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported: the provider is REST-only and needs a reachable server. Disclosure — all memory content (verbatim user and assistant turns) is stored in and read back from the Qdrant server at the configured url (default http://localhost:6333); QDRANT_API_KEY is only needed for Qdrant Cloud, is kept in .env and read through the Hermes secret scope, and is never written to config.yaml or qdrant.json. Disclosure — the only other outbound traffic is a one-time download of the embedding model weights from huggingface.co (fastembed falls back to storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed if that fails); embedding runs on-device and no memory content goes to any other party. Disclosure — settings are stored in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant.json (created 0600, no credentials) and last-operation status in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-status.json. Disclosure — md_search returns snippets of local markdown to the model from ~/.hermes/skills, the Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/hermes_default, ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/website and any path in the md_docs_roots key of qdrant.json; its index is built only when you run scripts/md_ingest.py and lives in <base Hermes home>/state/md-search/ (shared by all profiles). Disclosure — the optional semantic tier (md_ingest.py --semantic, and md_search queries with few lexical hits) sends embedding vectors plus file-path labels and section headings, never chunk text, to a separate hermes_md_docs collection on the Qdrant server named by the QDRANT_URL env var (default http://localhost:6333, no API key), and downloads paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 from huggingface.co on first use. Disclosure — the plugin is not a server and registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Hermes process that embeds, so each one pays its own model copy (measured ~194-211 MB per process).

name: quota
description: Per-provider quota / rate-limit status via /quota command and desktop widget. Reads precomputed quota_cache.json so the widget never does network I/O. Disclosure — refreshes your Gemini OAuth token using the Gemini CLI's public client identity, in memory only; queries Copilot's internal usage endpoint with VS Code client headers and Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint with a Claude Code User-Agent; the cursor check reads the Cursor CLI token from the macOS Keychain or Cursor's auth.json (read-only, never refreshed or rewritten; on expiry it asks you to run cursor-agent login) and queries api2.cursor.sh; the opt-in (default off) antigravity check reads Antigravity's OAuth token from Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli (read-only), refreshes it in memory with Antigravity's public client identity and sends Antigravity's User-Agent to Google's cloudcode endpoint; the opt-in (default off) grok.com check reads local browser cookies, using secret-tool on Linux or the macOS Keychain for the browser's Safe Storage key and decrypting only grok.com cookies from a temporary copy of the cookie DB; the opencode-go check reads the OpenCode CLI's local auth.json (read-only); the commandcode check reads ~/.commandcode/auth.json (read-only) or Hermes' credential store and uses the Command Code CLI's User-Agent; zai, kimi, minimax, deepseek and openrouter send keys from Hermes' credential store or env only to their own vendor's usage or balance endpoints.

name: reaction-feedback
description: Lets the agent see the emoji reactions you leave on its Telegram messages: react 👍 or 👎 to a reply and the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the message it followed. Disclosure — registers pre_gateway_dispatch (always returns None, so dispatch is never changed), pre_llm_call and gateway_platform_event hooks; keeps a bounded in-memory record of private-chat message ids, 60-character excerpts and reactions; writes nothing to disk, makes no network requests, starts no processes and reads no secrets.

name: reading-buddy
description: Local-first WeRead (微信读书) reading companion: syncs bookshelf, reading stats and notes to the local machine and turns them into private reading cards and weekly/monthly reviews through 8 MCP tools, with a built-in fictional demo mode for previews. Engine pinned to an immutable git commit (e5f6673) over npx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs Node.js 20+ on PATH. All data stays in PLUGIN_DATA; never posts to WeRead — cards and reviews are local files saved only after user confirmation. Disclosure — live mode sends your WEREAD_API_KEY as a Bearer token plus book ids and paging cursors to i.weread.qq.com (Tencent's WeRead agent gateway) and nothing else; the engine's MCP tool descriptions and error messages are Chinese-only while the skills are English-first; the engine's npm dependencies resolve as caret ranges at first launch.

name: reasoning-switch
description: Rotate the focused session reasoning effort from the status bar. A dialog sets the levels, colors, and per-level prompt limits. Disclosure — changes the focused session's reasoning effort through the gateway config.set API (core may fall back to writing the global config.yaml when the session id is stale) and auto-demotes the level after the configured number of prompts.

name: recency-anchor
description: Your system prompt is message zero and the user's question is message N. On models that weight recency hard, that is not a fair fight, and the instruction you care about most quietly loses to whatever was just asked. This plugin restates it at the end of every user turn instead. Append-only, API cop

name: remarkable
description: Unofficial reMarkable cloud transfers, library management, backups, typed text, and bounded native notebook rendering. Disclosure — talks to reMarkable cloud with a device token under ~/.hermes/credentials/remarkable/; remarkable_upload sends model-chosen local PDF/EPUB files to your account; the cloud sidecar (Node 22+) and renderer venv are installed only by the human-run setup commands; USB/SSH off by default.

name: reme
description: Local-first, file-native long-term memory with HTTP and embedded ReMe backends. Disclosure — search queries and full user/assistant turns are sent to the configured ReMe endpoint (default http://127.0.0.1:2333; a non-loopback http:// endpoint receives them in plaintext) or handled by the in-process ReMe SDK; no API keys are forwarded.

name: replaid
description: Connect Replaid with OAuth to read, triage, and draft replies in your social inbox.

name: rfc-ref
description: @rfc:<number> context references: attach an IETF RFC's record from the RFC Editor to a message (title, status, date, authors, abstract, what it obsoletes and updates and what obsoletes or updates it, errata link). Disclosure — sends one HTTPS GET per reference to www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc<number>.json only (the referenced RFC number leaves the machine); no API key, no caching, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @rfc: reference provider.

name: rocketchat-platform
description: Rocket.Chat gateway adapter for Hermes Agent. Connects to a self-hosted Rocket.Chat instance via the REST API v1 for outbound traffic and the Realtime (DDP) WebSocket for inbound messages. Uses aiohttp (already a Hermes dependency) — no extra packages needed.

name: rss-reader
description: Desktop RSS reader with reader-mode capture, drag-reorder subscriptions, mute rules, saved searches, AI summaries, keyboard shortcuts, and an optional headline ticker. Disclosure — optional YouTube cookies you paste in Settings are sent with YouTube feed requests; selectable User-Agent presets (incl. a ChatGPT-User string) are sent to feed hosts; YouTube videos render as youtube-nocookie.com embed iframes inside the reader.

name: rtk-rewrite-docker
description: Community plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) so the model sees compact output. Adds a backend gate: it rewrites only for terminal backends a profile opts in to (default local), so a Docker or remote backend without rtk never receives an rtk command. Fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout). Disclosure — every terminal command on an opted-in backend (default local) is passed to the rtk binary on the Hermes host's PATH (or RTK_BIN) and replaced with rtk's stdout before approval and execution; the plugin does not validate the rewrite, fails open on timeout or error, and downloads nothing (the repo's optional Containerfile fetches a checksum-pinned RTK release only when you build it). Not affiliated with rtk-ai.

name: rtk-rewrite
description: Community (non-official) plugin that rewrites Hermes terminal commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk, Apache-2.0) before execution, so the model sees compact output instead of raw command spam — cutting tokens on common dev commands. Adds a fail-open pre_tool_call hook (2s timeout, unexpected exits leave the command untouched), an optional desktop pane, and update scripts. Disclosure — every terminal tool command is passed to the rtk binary found on PATH (rtk-ai/rtk, installed separately) and replaced with rtk's rewrite before approval and execution; fail-open when rtk is missing or errors. Community mirror of upstream's hooks/hermes/rtk-rewrite, not affiliated with rtk-ai. scripts/update.sh downloads the pinned RTK release binary (v0.49.0, checksum-verified).

name: s3
description: Generic S3-compatible backup and restore operations for Hermes

name: sabi-metadata
description: Fail-closed attribution middleware for Sabi's local adaptive routing lane (sabi-code). Adds opaque session/turn headers on loopback only; ignores all other models. Verified on Hermes 0.21.3.

name: search1api
description: Live web search, news, page crawl, sitemap, and trending via Search1API

name: secret-drop
description: Store a secret on the gateway host without showing it to the model. Disclosure — stores the value in plaintext in the profile .env (mode 0600) and adds the name to terminal.env_passthrough, so $NAME is available to the terminal tool; the model can still read the value with its own tools (cat .env, echo $NAME). Keeps secrets out of chat/prompt context and redacts verbatim output of credential-shaped values; it is not a boundary against a model that deliberately reads it. Adds a static system-prompt section and a /secret command. Imports private core helpers read-only (_config_profile_scope, _is_hermes_provider_credential, _CONFIG_LOCK).

name: secret-handoff
description: Ephemeral credential paste: request_secret asks through clarify and injects the reply over CDP, never storing it. Disclosure — the password is collected through an ordinary unmasked clarify prompt, so it is visible in CLI scrollback and stays in messaging-platform chat history; it is typed over CDP only into a page whose origin matches the requested service.

name: secure-env-ingress
description: One-use HTTPS forms for missing environment secrets, native encrypted Browser Vault logins/TOTP setup keys, standalone verification codes, and approved secret operations outside chat and LLM input. Disclosure — /senv setup supplies a skill using sudo for host packages and TLS setup after approval; the TLS listener binds all interfaces by default; pre_gateway_dispatch observes gateway messages to bind commands to their sender. In interactive Telegram sessions, browser_vault saves logins or fills a code field through the captured browser supervisor without explicitly submitting the site form. Browser Use compatibility does not prove the latest named tab association. secure_operation executes administrator-allowlisted, SHA-256-pinned external Python consumers with gateway privileges; consumers are trusted, not sandboxed, and none are enabled by default. Secret input is not persisted by this mode; consumers must enforce their own handling policy. Links are bearer authorization, not submitter identity; cancellation cannot stop an already-running consumer.

name: sendblue
description: Sendblue iMessage / SMS integration. Provides typing indicators, async daemon routing, and Active LLM Tools for SMS dispatch.

name: serpapi
description: SerpApi web, Maps, News, Shopping, Hotels, Flights, and Travel Explore for Hermes Agent.
title: SerpApi

name: session-dashboard
description: Session Analyzer — per-session analytics for the Hermes desktop app: full page at /session-dashboard with token/cache/cost aggregates, tool-call breakdown, file changes, failure groups, and Ask AI (copies a ready-to-run analysis prompt into a fresh draft chat). Read-only over state.db.

name: session-ref
description: Reference another Hermes session in the Desktop composer with @session — type @ and pick from live session suggestions. Inserts a compact @session:"<title>" reference; nothing is injected into context, the agent resolves it with its own session-search. No more copying session IDs.

name: shodan
description: Shodan tools with complete capability declarations.

name: sidebar-cycle
description: Step through Hermes Desktop sidebar sessions in on-screen order with Ctrl+Cmd+] / Ctrl+Cmd+[ (rebindable), wrapping at both ends. SDK-only: session-row slot markers for order, host.state for the focused session, host.openSession for navigation.

name: sidebar-manager
description: Hide and reorder core sidebar navigation rows from a statusbar dialog.

name: sigrex
description: Build, run and manage sigrex.io trading automation (code and AI strategies, trading bots, webhooks and signals across crypto exchanges, DEXs and prediction markets) through the official Sigrex MCP server (Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.sigrex.io, OAuth sign-in, no keys in config), with the sigrex workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), no Python or executables; needs a free Sigrex account. The connection has full account access, including actions that can place live trades. Disclosure — the tool set is served by the remote MCP server at runtime and is not covered by the pinned sha; the bundled skill instructs the agent to confirm before any action that moves money or changes data.

name: sketch-pad
description: Draw a shape on a Desktop pad and attach the PNG to the next Hermes chat message. For "what is this shape" when you have no photo.

name: skill-retrieval
description: BM25-based skill retrieval for large skill libraries. An llm_request middleware rewrites the outgoing request's <available_skills> block to names only (the same bytes every turn, so prompt caching is unaffected), and a pre_llm_call hook appends the top-K matching skill descriptions to the current user message. Uses public plugin surfaces only (register_middleware, register_hook); reads SKILL.md frontmatter from the profile's skill roots and imports a few agent.prompt_builder / agent.skill_utils helpers read-only. pyyaml is the only dependency. Disclosure — optional Jev rerank, off by default: with SKILL_RETRIEVAL_RERANK=jev and TYPESAFE_API_KEY set (read from the environment only), each turn POSTs the user message (injection patterns stripped, capped at 2000 chars) and up to 12 shortlisted skill descriptions (400 chars each) to api.typesafe.ai (3 s timeout, no retries, BM25 order kept on error), and appends a local JSONL log (timestamp, session id, 200-char query excerpt, both orders) under $HERMES_HOME/data/jev-trial/, rotated past 5 MB. With the rerank off it makes no network calls and writes no files.

name: skill-router
description: Evidence-based, session-safe skill routing with auditable decisions and opt-in learning

name: snag-shelf
description: Everything that snagged - cross-session shelf of failed tool calls. Full Desktop page, chip, pin, fix-prompt insert. No API keys. Disclosure — stores failed tool-call metadata (tool, truncated args with key-name redaction, error snippet) locally in plugin-data; no network.

name: snyk
description: Scan code (SAST), dependencies, container images, IaC and SBOMs with Snyk through its first-party MCP server (pinned snyk@1.1306.0 over npx stdio, CLI analytics disabled), with the snyk-security-scan workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); needs Node.js/npm on PATH and a free Snyk account (browser login via the snyk_auth tool).

name: source-tray
description: Session source tray — URLs the Hermes agent opened via web_search, web_extract, or browser_navigate. Desktop pane and /sources. No search backend of its own and no API keys.

name: spectator
description: Harness-neutral live session sharing, summaries, and branch queries. Disclosure — reads state.db read-only and exposes masked transcripts to invite-token guests on the dashboard; host-approved guest suggestions are injected via ctx.inject_message.

name: spotify-desktop
description: Spotify Connect remote for Hermes Desktop — status-bar mini player (now playing, transport, volume, devices, search, playlists, queue) reusing the bundled Spotify auth (hermes auth spotify; Spotify Premium required for playback control). Unified agent+desktop package: Electron status-bar player plus a dashboard-API backend (desktop-focused, no web UI). No agent tools; config via plugins.entries.spotify-desktop.settings (poll intervals).

name: sticky-notes
description: In-window sticky notes for Hermes Desktop.

name: storm-fusion-research
description: Human-gated perspective-panel research. One question, several seats, one judge, one human. Solo, native subagent panel, or per-seat MoA/Fusion fanout via the storm_run_panel tool. Disclosure — every seat/judge call runs through Hermes's plugin LLM lane on your own credentials; with llm.allow_provider_override / allow_model_override enabled the agent picks provider and model per seat and spend follows that choice. The human gates are skill instructions to the agent, not enforced by the tool.

name: sugar
description: Local-first persistent memory for coding agents. SQLite on your disk - decisions, preferences, error patterns, and guidelines with project and global scopes and guideline-aware search. No cloud, no API key, nothing leaves the machine.

name: supermemory
description: Supermemory semantic long-term memory provider — profile recall, semantic search, explicit memory tools, and per-turn conversation capture. Maintained by Supermemory; the same provider that shipped in-tree.

name: t3-code-theme
description: Unofficial port of the standard T3 Code dark theme for Hermes Desktop. Palette, T3 composer, sidebar thread cards with project and branch, model labels and confirm dialogs. Scoped to its own theme; other themes are untouched. Disclosure — unofficial T3 Code lookalike theme; its stylesheet restyles and hides some native Desktop controls, it reads local session metadata (branch, repo, provider) for sidebar cards, and it switches the active theme once on first enable.
title: T3 Code Theme

name: tailgate
description: Per-job progress updates in chat for jobs Hermes hands off to other machines (coding agents, CI, scripts), with per-job mute and follow and no model calls.

name: talaria-webui
description: Extends Hermes Agent API capabilities to deliver a richer chat interface with Talaria WebUI. Disclosure — adds API_SERVER_KEY-authenticated /talaria/v1 routes to the Hermes API server (cross-session history search, rewind/branch/compress of API sessions, runs with the profile's instructions and prefill); stores response metadata (no message bodies) in $HERMES_HOME/talaria/observations.db; relies on private api_server/AIAgent internals behind feature detection.

name: tam
description: Local-first long-term memory backed by total-agent-memory (TAM) over MCP — saves each completed turn (with a noise filter; TAM's quality gate applies), recalls relevant memories before each turn within a token budget, and adds tam_recall / tam_save tools; optional TAM team server for shared company memory. Disclosure — local mode starts the separately installed tam binary as a child process per session with an allowlisted environment that carries no credentials: Hermes provider keys (including HF_TOKEN and OLLAMA_API_KEY), TAM_API_TOKEN and any *_TOKEN / *_API_KEY / *_SECRET / *_PASSWORD variable are withheld, and of HF_* / OLLAMA_* only non-secret settings pass (OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL, HF_HOME, HF_HUB_OFFLINE); it stores user/assistant turn text plus built-in memory additions (not tool output) in TAM's store, by default outside HERMES_HOME and shared with other agents using TAM; remote mode sends the same text to the user-configured URL with an optional TAM_API_TOKEN bearer token; hermes memory setup tam writes tam.json, TAM_API_TOKEN to .env and memory.provider in config.yaml.

name: tamahermes
description: Grow a local TamaHermes pet from real Hermes agent activity. Disclosure — hooks write a pet ledger and sprite atlas under $HERMES_HOME only; the optional python -m tamahermes CLI additionally reads/writes ~/.codex, ~/.petdex and ~/.evopet, runs an unauthenticated loopback preview server (127.0.0.1:8765) and on macOS compiles a Swift overlay and installs a RunAtLoad+KeepAlive LaunchAgent with no uninstall command. No network egress, no credential reads.

name: telegram-notify
description: Remote Telegram lifecycle notifications for the main Hermes agent: turn start, completion with a bounded final answer, interruption/failure, and user-facing approval requests. Suppresses subagent, Telegram-origin lifecycle, and automatic/smart-approval noise. Outbound-only, no input channel. Disclosure — enabled by default once installed and reuses the core Telegram gateway's TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL when present, so each main-agent turn's final answer (up to 3,200 chars) and approval-request command text (up to 700 chars) from CLI, Desktop and eligible gateway platforms are sent to api.telegram.org for delivery to that one chat; Telegram-origin lifecycle and approval-prompt copies (and, when notify_on_approval_response is enabled, Telegram-origin approval-response copies) are suppressed because the core Telegram gateway already delivers them in that chat; token and state are stored 0600 under HERMES_HOME/telegram-notify.

name: telegram_dashboard_probe
description: One pinned Telegram message with the state of your Hermes on one phone screen: gateway, backup, config drift, the cron ticker and its jobs, whether the Telegram channel is deaf, account limits and version. Read-only, no LLM calls, nothing to press. Disclosure — Claude and Codex limits come from Hermes' own account-usage fetcher, called every tick (which, like /usage, may refresh OAuth tokens through Hermes' own auth code); at most once per limits_refresh_seconds (default 900 s) the Grok weekly pool is read from https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing and /v1/settings with the xai-oauth token Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes request to xAI, may refresh that OAuth token and save it to auth.json, or clear a dead one, through Hermes' own auth code), sending the header x-xai-token-auth xai-grok-cli that identifies the request as the Grok CLI (an undocumented xAI host Hermes itself does not use), and Kimi Code windows from the kimi-coding base URL /v1/usages with the kimi-coding key Hermes resolves (which, like any Hermes key lookup without a usable key in .env or the environment, may save Hermes' credential pool back to auth.json once when loading it changes something, e.g. a placeholder key in .env) and a User-Agent of claude-code/0.1.0 (undocumented provider surfaces), and up to four operator-configured limits_sources, if set, each with one GET to http on loopback only (127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1), with no proxy and no redirect, optionally sending Authorization: Bearer with the value of an environment variable the operator names (never a *_BOT_TOKEN one); every tick the tail of HERMES_HOME/logs/errors.log (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) is read for Gemini HTTP 429 lines, of which only the time, limit, retry and model are kept, and for the engine's own 'Failed to send Telegram message' lines, of which only the time is kept, never the message text; every tick HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never prompt, script, deliver, skills or the model) and the ticker's marker files for their epoch, and HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db is opened read-only (sqlite3 mode=ro with PRAGMA query_only, in a worker under the tick's deadline) for the job_id, status, delivery_outcome and time columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the error column; the engine's error texts are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the record; the connected Telegram adapter's public property send_path_degraded is read every tick, and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (_updates_received_total, _polling_generation, _polling_last_progress_monotonic, _polling_generation_started_monotonic) are read as attributes, nothing is called on it, and an adapter without them shows no data for that line; the plugin's own code never reads the Telegram bot token and never writes vendor credential files (Hermes' auth code it calls for Grok and Kimi may, as said above), and no request the plugin's own code sends with a token in a header follows a redirect; the latest Hermes release list is read from api.github.com without a token at most once a day; an operator-configured drift_command, if set, runs as a subprocess; the delivery record is written under HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/.
title: Telegram Dashboard

name: telnyx-provider
description: Vendor-maintained Telnyx inference provider with an authenticated live model catalog, hosted open models, frontier routes, and catalog-derived pricing.

name: thomas
description: Fine-tune a small calibrated encoder classifier on Modal and rate it with gonogo. Every GPU launch goes through the human approval gate with the exact config shown; data checks and evaluation run locally for free. Training and inference run in a separate Python interpreter the user configures via THOMAS_PYTHON (with the author's thomas package, torch and modal installed); the Hermes venv only gets gonogo-eval. Runs and artifacts are written under HERMES_HOME/thomas/runs; the eval tool writes report files to the path the model supplies.

name: time-gap
description: Inject an implicit time-gap sense only when a gap or a date rollover crosses.

name: titanos-mcp
description: Connect Hermes to Titanos marketplace, Amazon, listings, Ads, and product research tools through the pinned Titanos OAuth MCP client. This portable Agent Plugin v1 package bundles seven operating skills, requires Node.js 20.18.1 or newer, and uses browser authorization with a Titanos account. Disclosure — starts the npm package @titanos/mcp-agents@1.47.2 via npx (fetched from npm on first run); its tools read and WRITE live marketplace/Ads accounts under your Titanos OAuth session.

name: tokenwatch
description: Monitor Hermes token usage, notify at thresholds, and freeze tool/gateway activity at configured limits.

name: tool-slimmer
description: Reduce Hermes tool-schema overhead and show selector savings in the dashboard. Disclosure — optional mode jev (off by default; needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY) sends each turn's request text and up to 32 candidate tool names and descriptions to TypeSafe (api.typesafe.ai); all other modes run locally. Optional user-run scripts can patch Hermes core on older Hermes and install a systemd user self-heal unit; the dashboard advisor edits the tool_slimmer section of config.yaml with a backup.

name: toolaria
description: Rescues oversized MCP and web tool results before they flood context.

name: touchdesigner
description: Drive a live TouchDesigner session through the twozero MCP server (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:40404), with the touchdesigner-mcp workflow skill bundled. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/); TouchDesigner itself runs on macOS/Windows.

name: turn-bell
description: A bell in the Hermes desktop composer that pings the ntfy topic Hermes already uses when a turn finishes. Click to cycle off, current turn, or all turns. Disclosure — when enabled, posts the first line of each finished reply plus model, duration, token and cost figures to the ntfy server/topic Hermes is configured with (default ntfy.sh); reads NTFY_* from the profile .env and falls back to the ntfy CLI's ~/.config/ntfy/client.yml login (read-only).

name: turn-usage
description: Usage and cost footer appended to every reply — tokens, cache hit rate, cost and context occupancy, plus a per-tool time breakdown showing which tool actually consumed the wall clock. Waiting time (a blocking user prompt) is reported separately and excluded from the active-time denominator. Pure computation, never calls a model; any failure leaves the reply untouched. Disclosure — the usage footer is appended to the stored assistant reply, so it is replayed to the model on later turns and adds tokens to every turn.

name: twenty-crm
description: Twenty CRM for Hermes Agent with managed self-hosting, external-instance connectivity, REST, GraphQL, and live schema introspection.

name: typesafe-skill-router
description: TypeSafe (Jev) skill routing: the request is routed before the model call and the one skill from the live roster that fits it is named in a single <skill_relevance> line on the user message — nothing is injected when nothing fits.

name: umt
description: Connect 28 production-ready MCP servers to any coding agent. Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/): three zero-config stdio servers out of the box (Hacker News, arXiv, npm registry, each pinned to an exact npm version), plus the umt-mcp skill that drives the umt CLI to wire any of the 28 servers into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed and more. Needs Node.js and npm on PATH.

name: unbrowse
description: Unbrowse: websites as APIs. Read any page as clean markdown, run tasks on sites through learned first-party APIs (no browser), and drive a cloud browser with saved logins when nothing matches. Also a web_extract backend and a guard that routes public-web browser_* calls to Unbrowse. Disclosure — hosted service: page URLs, task text and tool arguments are sent to unbrowse.ai with your API key, pages are fetched and site logins are stored on Unbrowse's side, and verified calls bill the Unbrowse account; once UNBROWSE_API_KEY is set the plugin blocks the built-in browser_* tools and web_extract on public URLs by default (settings blockBrowser/blockWebExtract, or UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1).

name: unitares
description: Records each Hermes session on a UNITARES server you run: one identity per session and one check-in per completed turn, so the agent's working record carries across sessions. Fail-open; never blocks the agent. Disclosure — sends only to the server named in UNITARES_MCP_URL, which you host; there is no default server. Per session it sends your model name and platform; per completed turn a fixed check-in marker (never user, assistant or tool text). Hooks run synchronously, so an unresponsive server can add up to ~40 s per call until the plugin auto-disables after 3 consecutive failures.

name: usage-ledger
description: Local-only content-free usage tally and native Desktop statusline (Windows beta).

name: usage-stats
description: Multi-provider usage/balance for the Hermes Desktop status bar — shows live usage for OpenCode, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, NovitaAI, ZAI, Alibaba, Arcee, plus gateway-native Claude/Codex/Cursor/Nous.

name: vault-view
description: Local Markdown vault workspace for Hermes Desktop: visual editing, progressive reading, cached image previews, shared tabs, tag search, links, backlinks and a graph. Compatible with Obsidian vaults. File transport requires a Linux/macOS gateway; Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend, not a native Windows gateway; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Remote images and agent guidance are opt-in and disabled by default; automatic note-content sharing is disabled; direct Obsidian opening is temporarily hidden. Disclosure — reads and writes notes in the vault folder you choose through Desktop shell commands on the gateway host; remote Markdown images and agent navigation guidance stay off until you opt in.
title: Vault View

name: vaultknox
description: Secret-leak protection for Hermes chats. Scans inbound messages and outbound replies for API keys, tokens, and passwords with a 28-pattern detector registry, redacts them before they reach session storage or the user, and injects safe secret-handling rules so the agent never asks for secrets in chat. Zero dependencies, fully offline detection; pairs with the optional hermes-vault CLI for encrypted storage. Disclosure — rewrites inbound user messages (regex secret redaction, may false-positive on password-like strings), injects a secret-handling prompt each conversation and rewrites assistant replies that ask for secrets; outbound replies are value-redacted with the same registry (regex-based, so a shape no detector covers passes through), with findings logged as detector name plus SHA-256 fingerprint and never the raw value. The vaultknox tool is inert unless the separate vaultknox pip package is installed, its write gate is a tool argument the model sets, and a vault policy that authorises raw consume_token returns the plaintext to the model.

name: vaultwarden
description: Vaultwarden / Bitwarden Password Manager (bw CLI) secret source

name: vector-platform
description: Vector (vectorapp.io) messaging platform plugin: Hermes becomes a first-class Nostr-based Vector bot (its own nsec/npub identity), relaying DMs through a local Rust sidecar that wraps vector-sdk. First run needs `hermes gateway setup`, which provisions the bot identity (create or import). Disclosure — `hermes gateway setup` downloads a prebuilt vector-bridge binary from github.com/BonesGit/hermes-vector-platform/releases (tag v<version>, sha256 checked against that release's SHA256SUMS; set vector.prebuilt.download: false to build from the bundled Rust source), merges `vector:` settings into ~/.hermes/config.yaml, writes VECTOR_* to ~/.hermes/.env, and publishes a public bot profile (kind-0, bot: true) to Nostr discovery relays.

name: vet402
description: Look a paid x402 or MPP URL up in vet402's public record of real purchases before the agent pays it. BLOCK stops the tool call, and a WARN backed by evidence against the seller asks for approval. Disclosure — sends each guarded or model-queried URL (scheme, host and path; userinfo, query and fragment stripped) to vet402.com in up to two HTTPS GETs; fails open, so a vet402 outage or unknown URL lets the payment run unless VET402_UNKNOWN=approve.

name: vidiq
description: Grow on YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok with vidIQ. Disclosure — skills only; you add vidIQ's hosted MCP server yourself with hermes mcp add vidiq --url https://mcp.vidiq.com/mcp --auth oauth; tool calls send your prompts and authorized channel data to vidIQ and spend vidIQ account credits.

name: vk-platform
description: VK Messenger gateway with community Long Poll, media attachments, allowlists, and project-lane routing.

name: vornik-companion
description: Vornik as Hermes's hardened broker and long-term memory: Hermes holds no credentials; privileged work runs in operator-approved workflows on your own Vornik daemon. Disclosure — talks only to the self-hosted Vornik daemon at VORNIK_URL with VORNIK_BROKER_TOKEN; broker tools let the agent start operator-approved workflows on that daemon (writes are approved by a person in Vornik); when selected as memory provider it sends each turn's user query for recall and mirrors MEMORY.md and USER.md writes to the daemon; hermes vornik connect runs the local vornikctl, which adds an MCP entry to Hermes config.

name: watchline
description: Watchline delivery adapter for Hermes Agent. Polls a Watchline pull channel and forwards matched events into the Hermes gateway as inbound messages.

name: weather
description: Weather data, radar/model imagery, and verified meteorological calculations. Built on metrust, rusbie, wrf-rust, rustdar, and ecape-rs.

name: web-defuddle
description: Defuddle content extraction — local, free, no API key. Shells out to the defuddle CLI for clean article markdown. Extract-only; pair with SearXNG or another search provider.

name: web-meta-ai
description: Meta web search — routes web_search through the server-side web_search tool on Meta's Responses API (Muse Spark); search-only. Disclosure — each search is a separate billed Meta Model API call (per-query web search fee plus tokens) on MODEL_API_KEY.

name: web-octen
description: Octen web search with query-focused highlights and page extraction.

name: web-ollama-cloud
description: Ollama Cloud web search + content extraction via Ollama's native REST API. Search returns web results; extract fetches page content. Reuses OLLAMA_API_KEY (https://ollama.com/settings/keys).

name: web-oxylabs
description: Oxylabs AI Studio web search and extraction provider for Hermes Agent. Requires OXYLABS_API_KEY (sign up at https://aistudio.oxylabs.io/api-key).

name: web-search-plus
description: Multi-provider web search, URL extraction, quality reports, and opt-in research mode. Disclosure — reads the operator's HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (read-only) for its own Desktop settings block (country, language, max_results, auto_routing, searxng_url); may spawn its own search.py and an operator-configured local donsetch CLI as subprocesses (argv, no shell).

name: web-serply
description: Serply web search provider for Hermes Agent. Google web results via the Serply SERP API. Requires SERPLY_API_KEY (sign up at https://serply.io).

name: web-toon
description: Paid web extract over TOON: web_extract pays a TOON node about $0.001 per page from a local payer sidecar; the node fetches through an Anyone network exit and returns markdown with a wuzzy/crawl v1 content hash. Disclosure — with TOON_PAYER_URL set and web.extract_backend toon, every web_extract URL goes to the user's anonfetch payer sidecar and spends about $0.001 from its TOON payment channel with no per-call confirmation; the sidecar's daily cap and origin allowlist are the only spending controls; pages are fetched through Anyone network exits.

name: web-venice
description: Venice AI web search + extract — privacy-first, zero data retention, $0.01/request.

name: wechat-social-assistant
description: Local-first WeChat relationship memory assistant for macOS: captures only what is visible in the WeChat window via system OCR/Accessibility, stores everything in a local SQLite database (0600/0700 permissions, no cloud), and serves contact briefs, follow-up planning, outreach drafts and weekly relationship reports through 32 MCP tools. Engine pinned to the immutable PyPI release wechat-social-assistant==1.5.1 over uvx stdio; Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/), needs uv on PATH. All data confined to PLUGIN_DATA via WSA_ALLOWED_ROOT + path enforcement. Never reads WeChat databases, never injects into WeChat, never sends messages — outreach is drafts for human review only. Disclosure — reads WeChat only by screenshotting/OCR-ing and walking the macOS Accessibility tree of the frontmost window (not WeChat's databases or a bot API), compiles bundled Swift helpers with swiftc into ~/Library/Caches/wechat-social-assistant/bin on first use, and needs Screen Recording (optionally Accessibility) permission for the host terminal; no network egress, never sends messages.

name: whatsapp-agent-platform
description: Community platform plugin (not affiliated with Meta or Nous Research) connecting a WhatsApp Agent to Hermes through Meta's WhatsApp Agent Platform API (/agent/v1): long-poll inbound (no public URL), text and media. Disclosure — sends the API key and message content, files included, only to Meta: api.whatsapp.com, plus lookaside.fbsbx.com for downloads (per WhatsApp's Third-Party Agents Terms, agent chats are not end-to-end encrypted); stores the poll cursor, recent message ids and the creator's id under HERMES_HOME; no other network egress, no telemetry, no self-update. Exception: Hermes fetches image URLs in replies (SSRF-guarded, no key), revealing the server's IP to that host. Files go only to the creator; Meta keeps uploads up to 30 days. Received files are cached under HERMES_HOME (deleted after ~24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider. WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false disables media. By default only the agent's creator (verified through Meta's API) can message Hermes; WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOWED_USERS or WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS widens that explicitly. The agent API key is saved to the Hermes .env; the state file under HERMES_HOME is 0600 and never contains the key.
title: WhatsApp Agent Platform

name: wiki-ref
description: @wiki:<title> context references: attach the lead section of a Wikipedia article to a message, or one section with @wiki:<title>#<section>, with title autocomplete in the TUI and Desktop composer. Disclosure — sends HTTPS GET requests to <language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php only (the referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine; a section is cut locally); no API key, no files written, no subprocess; register() only adds the @wiki: reference provider.

name: woof
description: Plan, launch, watch and compare WOOF weather simulations on your own NVIDIA GPU: size runs with WOOF's own planner, launch them locally or on an ssh/WSL GPU host, get maps in the chat while the forecast runs, compare physics or resolution, run multi-arm research campaigns and score runs against radar and surface observations. Disclosure — runs need Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU (plan-only elsewhere); the user-run hermes woof install pip-installs recast-woof>=1.0.0,<1.1 into ~/woof-env and downloads WOOF tables and optional geography (about 1.6 GB); runs execute the WOOF CLI as detached background jobs writing to ~/woof-runs and fetch public weather data; run events are pushed into the chat as user-role messages; the optional serve/ scripts download llama.cpp and a Qwen GGUF and start an unauthenticated local model server.

name: xmemo
description: Native XMemo memory provider for Hermes Agent — durable, identity-aware cross-session memory with semantic search. Disclosure — cloud memory provider: sends each user prompt (for recall), model-written memories and mirrored built-in Hermes memory writes, plus a stable install ID, to xmemo.dev (Yonro Co., Ltd.); reuses the xmemo login token from ~/.config/xmemo if present.

name: yantrikdb-hermes-dashboard
description: Local-only YantrikDB dashboard for Hermes Agent memory operations

name: yantrikdb
description: Persistent memory for Hermes. Canonicalizes duplicate memories, surfaces contradictions between structured or recognized single-valued claims for review, and returns a why_retrieved reason list with every recall. Embedded by default: no server, no token, no GPU. Optional HTTP backend for HA clusters; pluggable embedders (bundled potion-2M default).

name: yolo-auto
description: Yolo-Auto: flat-rate OpenAI-compatible API with plan-filtered live model discovery.

name: you
description: You.com skills for live web search, URL content extraction, cited research, finance research, and integration discovery via the You.com MCP servers (api.you.com). Portable Agent Plugins v1 package (mcp.json + skills/, five skills bundled); auth via YDC_API_KEY, OAuth, or MPP/x402 — the free profile works keyless.

name: zerosignal
description: ZeroSignal — private, pay-per-request inference through the local zs-proxy; no API key, your wallet is the credential.
